# dlaebz

> Computes the number of eigenvalues of a real symmetric tridiagonal matrix which are less than or equal to a given value, and performs other tasks required by the routine sstebz.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaebz from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaebz';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaebz(
    order,
    ijob, nitmax,
    N, mmax, minp,
    nbmin, abstol, reltol, pivmin,
    d, strideD,
    e, strideE,
    E2, strideE2,
    NVAL, strideNVAL,
    AB, LDAB,
    c, strideC,
    mout,
    NAB, LDNAB,
    WORK,
    IWORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `ijob` | `integer` | in |  |  | specifies what is to be done: = 1: Compute NAB for the initial intervals. = 2: Perform bisection iteration to find eigenvalues of T. = 3: Perform bisection iteration to invert N(w), i.e., to find a point which has a specified number of eigenvalues of T to its left. |
| `nitmax` | `integer` | in |  |  | the maximum number of "levels" of bisection to be performed, i.e., an interval of width W will not be made smaller than 2^(-NITMAX) * W. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the dimension n of the tridiagonal matrix T. |
| `mmax` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the maximum number of intervals. |
| `minp` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the initial number of intervals. |
| `nbmin` | `integer` | in |  |  | the smallest number of intervals that should be processed using a vector loop. |
| `abstol` | `number` | in |  |  | the minimum (absolute) width of an interval. |
| `reltol` | `number` | in |  |  | the minimum relative width of an interval. |
| `pivmin` | `number` | in |  |  | the minimum absolute value of a "pivot" in the Sturm sequence loop. |
| `d` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | the diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T. |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | the offdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T in positions 1 through N-1. |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `e` |
| `E2` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | the squares of the offdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T. |
| ↳ `strideE2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `E2` |
| `NVAL` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `minp` |  | if IJOB=1 or 2, not referenced (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideNVAL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `NVAL` |
| `AB` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `mmax × 2` |  | the endpoints of the intervals. |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `AB` |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `mmax` |  | if IJOB=1, ignored. |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `c` |
| `mout` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | if IJOB=1, the number of eigenvalues in the intervals. |
| `NAB` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `mmax × 2` |  | if IJOB=1, then on output NAB(i,j) will be set to N(AB(i,j)). |
| ↳ `LDNAB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `NAB` |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ mmax` |  | caller-provided workspace of at least `mmax` elements |
| `IWORK` | `(Int32Array\|null)` | out | `≥ mmax` |  | caller-provided workspace of at least `mmax` elements |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `ijob`: Specifies what is to be done:

  -   `= 1`: Compute `NAB` for the initial intervals.
  -   `= 2`: Perform bisection iteration to find eigenvalues of T.
  -   `= 3`: Perform bisection iteration to invert `N(w)`, i.e., to find a point which has a specified number of eigenvalues of T to its left. Other values will cause DLAEBZ to return with `INFO=-1`.
- `nitmax`: The maximum number of "levels" of bisection to be performed, i.e., an interval of width W will not be made smaller than 2^$(-\mathrm{NITMAX}) \, W$. If not all intervals have converged after `NITMAX` iterations, then `INFO` is set to the number of non-converged intervals.
- `N`: The dimension n of the tridiagonal matrix T. It must be at least 1.
- `mmax`: The maximum number of intervals. If more than `MMAX` intervals are generated, then DLAEBZ will quit with $\mathrm{INFO}=\mathrm{MMAX}+1$.
- `minp`: The initial number of intervals. It may not be greater than `MMAX`.
- `nbmin`: The smallest number of intervals that should be processed using a vector loop. If zero, then only the scalar loop will be used.
- `abstol`: The minimum (absolute) width of an interval. When an interval is narrower than `ABSTOL`, or than `RELTOL` times the larger (in magnitude) endpoint, then it is considered to be sufficiently small, i.e., converged. This must be at least zero.
- `reltol`: The minimum relative width of an interval. When an interval is narrower than `ABSTOL`, or than `RELTOL` times the larger (in magnitude) endpoint, then it is considered to be sufficiently small, i.e., converged. Note: this should always be at least radix\*machine $\epsilon$.
- `pivmin`: The minimum absolute value of a "pivot" in the Sturm sequence loop. This must be at least max \|$e(j)^2$\|\*safe\_min and at least safe\_min, where safe\_min is at least the smallest number that can divide one without overflow.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `e`: The offdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T in positions 1 through N-1. `E(N)` is arbitrary.
- `E2`: The squares of the offdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T. `E2(N)` is ignored.
- `NVAL`: If `IJOB=1` or 2, not referenced. If `IJOB=3`, the desired values of `N(w)`. The elements of `NVAL` will be reordered to correspond with the intervals in `AB`. Thus, `NVAL(j)` on output will not, in general be the same as `NVAL(j)` on input, but it will correspond with the interval (`AB(j,1)`,`AB(j,2)`\] on output.
- `AB`: The endpoints of the intervals. `AB(j,1)` is a(j), the left endpoint of the j-th interval, and `AB(j,2)` is b(j), the right endpoint of the j-th interval. The input intervals will, in general, be modified, split, and reordered by the calculation.
- `c`: If `IJOB=1`, ignored. If `IJOB=2`, workspace. If `IJOB=3`, then on input `C(j)` should be initialized to the first search point in the binary search.
- `mout`: If `IJOB=1`, the number of eigenvalues in the intervals. If `IJOB=2` or 3, the number of intervals output. If `IJOB=3`, `MOUT` will equal `MINP`.
- `NAB`: If `IJOB=1`, then on output `NAB(i,j)` will be set to `N(AB(i,j))`. If `IJOB=2`, then on input, `NAB(i,j)` should be set. It must

  -   satisfy the condition:
  -   $N(\mathrm{AB}(i,1)) \le \mathrm{NAB}(i,1) \le \mathrm{NAB}(i,2) \le N(\mathrm{AB}(i,2))$,
  -   which means that in interval i only eigenvalues
  -   `NAB(i,1)`+1,...,`NAB(i,2)` will be considered. Usually,
  -   `NAB(i,j)=N(AB(i,j))`, from a previous call to DLAEBZ with
  -   `IJOB=1`.
  -   On output, `NAB(i,j)` will contain
  -   max(na(k),min(nb(k),`N(AB(i,j))`)), where k is the index of
  -   the input interval that the output interval
  -   (`AB(j,1)`,`AB(j,2)`\] came from, and na(k) and nb(k) are the
  -   the input values of `NAB(k,1)` and `NAB(k,2)`.

  If `IJOB=3`, then on output, `NAB(i,j)` contains `N(AB(i,j))`,

  -   unless $N(w) > \mathrm{NVAL}(i)$ for all search points w , in which
  -   case `NAB(i,1)` will not be modified, i.e., the output
  -   value will be the same as the input value (modulo
  -   reorderings -- see `NVAL` and `AB`), or unless $N(w) < \mathrm{NVAL}(i)$
  -   for all search points w , in which case `NAB(i,2)` will
  -   not be modified. Normally, `NAB` should be set to some
  -   distinctive value(s) before DLAEBZ is called.
- `WORK`: Workspace.
- `IWORK`: Workspace.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaebz.ndarray(
    ijob, nitmax,
    N, mmax, minp,
    nbmin, abstol, reltol, pivmin,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    e, strideE, offsetE,
    E2, strideE2, offsetE2,
    NVAL, strideNVAL, offsetNVAL,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    c, strideC, offsetC,
    mout,
    NAB, strideNAB1, strideNAB2, offsetNAB,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork
) → integer
```

Computes the number of eigenvalues of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix T.
less than or equal to a given value, and performs bisection iteration.

IJOB=1: Compute NAB for the initial intervals.
IJOB=2: Perform bisection iteration to find eigenvalues of T.
IJOB=3: Perform bisection iteration to invert N(w).

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ijob` | `integer` | in |  |  | specifies what is to be done (1, 2, or 3) |
| `nitmax` | `integer` | in |  |  | maximum number of bisection levels |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | dimension of the tridiagonal matrix |
| `mmax` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | maximum number of intervals |
| `minp` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | initial number of intervals |
| `nbmin` | `integer` | in |  |  | smallest number of intervals for vector loop |
| `abstol` | `number` | in |  |  | minimum absolute width of an interval |
| `reltol` | `number` | in |  |  | minimum relative width of an interval |
| `pivmin` | `number` | in |  |  | minimum absolute value of a pivot |
| `d` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | diagonal elements, length N |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for d |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for d |
| `e` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | off-diagonal elements, length N |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for e |
| ↳ `offsetE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for e |
| `E2` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | squares of off-diagonal elements, length N |
| ↳ `strideE2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for E2 |
| ↳ `offsetE2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for E2 |
| `NVAL` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `minp` |  | desired eigenvalue counts (IJOB=3 only) |
| ↳ `strideNVAL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for NVAL |
| ↳ `offsetNVAL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for NVAL |
| `AB` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `mmax × 2` |  | interval endpoints, shape [MMAX, 2] |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | first dimension stride for AB |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | second dimension stride for AB |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for AB |

| ↳ `strideNAB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | first dimension stride for NAB |
| ↳ `strideNAB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | second dimension stride for NAB |
| ↳ `offsetNAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for NAB |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ mmax` |  | workspace, length MMAX |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WORK |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array` | out | `≥ mmax` |  | workspace, length MMAX |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IWORK |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for IWORK |

**Returns** `integer`: info: 0=all converged, 1..MMAX=non-converged count, MMAX+1=overflow

**Throws**

- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `mmax` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `ijob < 1 || ijob > 3`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: All intervals converged. = 1--`MMAX`: The last `INFO` intervals did not converge. = `MMAX`+1:  More than `MMAX` intervals were generated.

</section>

## Notes

-   `dlaebz()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAEBZ`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlaebz.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dlaebz from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaebz';

// 3x3 symmetric tridiagonal matrix T with diagonal `d` and off-diagonal `e` (all eigenvalues lie in [-5, 5]):
var N = 3;
var MMAX = 8;
var PIVMIN = 2.2250738585072014e-308;
var d = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, -1.0, 3.0 ] );
var e = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0, 0.0 ] );
var E2 = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0, 0.0 ] );
var NVAL = new Int32Array( MMAX );
var AB = new Float64Array( MMAX * 2 );
var NAB = new Int32Array( MMAX * 2 );
var c = new Float64Array( MMAX );
var mout = new Int32Array( 1 );
var WORK = new Float64Array( MMAX );
var IWORK = new Int32Array( MMAX );
var i;

// Using the standard interface: count the eigenvalues in [-5, 5] (IJOB=1), then bisect (IJOB=2):
AB[ 0 ] = -5.0;
AB[ MMAX ] = 5.0;
dlaebz( 'column-major', 1, 0, N, MMAX, 1, 0, 0.0, 0.0, PIVMIN, d, 1, e, 1, E2, 1, NVAL, 1, AB, MMAX, c, 1, mout, NAB, MMAX, WORK, IWORK );
console.log( 'eigenvalues in [-5, 5]:', NAB[ MMAX ] - NAB[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

var info = dlaebz( 'column-major', 2, 60, N, MMAX, 1, 0, 1.0e-12, 1.0e-12, PIVMIN, d, 1, e, 1, E2, 1, NVAL, 1, AB, MMAX, c, 1, mout, NAB, MMAX, WORK, IWORK );
console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
for ( i = 0; i < mout[ 0 ]; i++ ) {
	console.log( 'interval %d: [%d, %d] holds %d eigenvalue(s)', i, AB[ i ], AB[ MMAX + i ], NAB[ MMAX + i ] - NAB[ i ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
}

// Using the ndarray interface: count the eigenvalues in [-5, 0] and [0, 5] (IJOB=1):
AB[ 0 ] = -5.0;
AB[ MMAX ] = 0.0;
AB[ 1 ] = 0.0;
AB[ MMAX + 1 ] = 5.0;
dlaebz.ndarray( 1, 0, N, MMAX, 2, 0, 0.0, 0.0, PIVMIN, d, 1, 0, e, 1, 0, E2, 1, 0, NVAL, 1, 0, AB, 1, MMAX, 0, c, 1, 0, mout, NAB, 1, MMAX, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( 'eigenvalues in [-5, 0]:', NAB[ MMAX ] - NAB[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'eigenvalues in [0, 5]:', NAB[ MMAX + 1 ] - NAB[ 1 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAEBZ`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLAEBZ contains the iteration loops which compute and use the function `N(w)`, which is the count of eigenvalues of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix T less than or equal to its argument w. It performs a choice of two types of loops:

`IJOB=1`, followed by `IJOB=2`: It takes as input a list of intervals and returns a list of

-   sufficiently small intervals whose union contains the same
-   eigenvalues as the union of the original intervals.
-   The input intervals are (`AB(j,1)`,`AB(j,2)`\], $j=1$,...,`MINP`.
-   The output interval (`AB(j,1)`,`AB(j,2)`\] will contain
-   eigenvalues `NAB(j,1)`+1,...,`NAB(j,2)`, where $1 \le j \le \mathrm{MOUT}$.

`IJOB=3`: It performs a binary search in each input interval

-   (`AB(j,1)`,`AB(j,2)`\] for a point w(j) such that
-   $N(w(j))=\mathrm{NVAL}(j)$, and uses `C(j)` as the starting point of
-   the search. If such a w(j) is found, then on output
-   `AB(j,1)=AB(j,2)=w`. If no such w(j) is found, then on output
-   (`AB(j,1)`,`AB(j,2)`\] will be a small interval containing the
-   point where `N(w)` jumps through `NVAL(j)`, unless that point
-   lies outside the initial interval.

Note that the intervals are in all cases half-open intervals, i.e., of the form (a,b\] , which includes b but not a .

To avoid underflow, the matrix should be scaled so that its largest element is no greater than overflow\*\*(1/2) \* underflow\*\*(1/4) in absolute value. To assure the most accurate computation of small eigenvalues, the matrix should be scaled to be not much smaller than that, either.

See W. Kahan "Accurate Eigenvalues of a Symmetric Tridiagonal Matrix", Report CS41, Computer Science Dept., Stanford University, July 21, 1966

Note: the arguments are, in general, \*not\* checked for unreasonable values.

### Further Details

This routine is intended to be called only by other LAPACK routines, thus the interface is less user-friendly. It is intended for two purposes:

(a) finding eigenvalues. In this case, DLAEBZ should have one or

-   more initial intervals set up in `AB`, and DLAEBZ should be called
-   with `IJOB=1`. This sets up `NAB`, and also counts the eigenvalues.
-   Intervals with no eigenvalues would usually be thrown out at
-   this point. Also, if not all the eigenvalues in an interval i
-   are desired, `NAB(i,1)` can be increased or `NAB(i,2)` decreased.
-   For example, set $\mathrm{NAB}(i,1)=\mathrm{NAB}(i,2)-1$ to get the largest
-   eigenvalue. DLAEBZ is then called with `IJOB=2` and `MMAX`
-   no smaller than the value of `MOUT` returned by the call with
-   `IJOB=1`. After this (`IJOB`=2) call, eigenvalues `NAB(i,1)`+1
-   through `NAB(i,2)` are approximately `AB(i,1)` (or `AB(i,2)`) to the
-   tolerance specified by `ABSTOL` and `RELTOL`.

(b) finding an interval (a',b'\] containing eigenvalues w(f),...,w(l).

-   In this case, start with a Gershgorin interval (a,b). Set up
-   `AB` to contain 2 search intervals, both initially (a,b). One
-   `NVAL` element should contain f-1 and the other should contain l
-   , while C should contain a and b, resp. `NAB(i,1)` should be -1
-   and `NAB(i,2)` should be N+1, to flag an error if the desired
-   interval does not lie in (a,b). DLAEBZ is then called with
-   `IJOB=3`. On exit, if $w(f-1) < w(f)$, then one of the intervals --
-   j -- will have `AB(j,1)=AB(j,2)` and $\mathrm{NAB}(j,1)=\mathrm{NAB}(j,2)=f-1$, while
-   if, to the specified tolerance, w(f-k)=...=w(f+r), $k > 0$ and r
-   \>= 0, then the interval will have $N(\mathrm{AB}(j,1))=\mathrm{NAB}(j,1)=f-k$ and
-   $N(\mathrm{AB}(j,2))=\mathrm{NAB}(j,2)=f+r$. The cases $w(l) < w(l+1)$ and
-   w(l-r)=...=w(l+k) are handled similarly.

</section>
